Wizard.logoHint: PNG, JPG or WebP, max 1 MB

Wizard.revenueIntro: We only accept a read-only Stripe restricted key. It is encrypted, never shown again, and you can revoke it in Stripe any time.
Wizard.howTo1: Click the button below → name the key, e.g. JaoPor
Wizard.howTo2: Set Charges → Read and Subscriptions → Read (leave the rest as None)
Wizard.howTo3: Click Create key → copy the key starting with rk_ → paste it below

Wizard.limitReached: You can list up to 5 startups.
Wizard.basicsIntro: Takes under a minute — one link is enough. Everything else can be added later from your profile.

Wizard.skipVerify: Not ready? Skip for now and verify later from the edit page.

Sources.title: Verify your numbers
Sources.intro: Read-only connections. Keys are encrypted and never shown again; numbers refresh daily. Pick at least one.
Sources.revenueHint: Web SaaS → Stripe · Mobile apps → RevenueCat
Sources.trafficHint: Real visitors from your site's analytics (must be the same domain as your website).
Sources.buildHint: Commits, first commit and the share co-authored with Claude, from a public repo.
Sources.disconnectConfirm: Disconnect {source}? Its verified numbers will be removed.
Sources.success: Verified! The numbers are on your profile now.

stripe.howTo1: Click the button below → name the key, e.g. JaoPor
stripe.howTo2: Set Charges → Read and Subscriptions → Read (leave the rest as None)
stripe.howTo3: Click Create key → copy the key starting with rk_ → paste it below

revenuecat.howTo1: RevenueCat → Project settings → API keys → + New secret API key → choose V2
revenuecat.howTo2: Set Charts & metrics → Read only, and every other area → No access
revenuecat.howTo3: Copy the sk_… key and the Project ID (in the URL: app.revenuecat.com/projects/<ID>/…)

plausible.howTo1: Plausible → Account settings → API keys → New API key → choose Stats API
plausible.howTo2: Paste the key, and check the domain matches the one shown in Plausible

umami.howTo1: Umami → Websites → Edit → turn on Share URL
umami.howTo2: Paste the …/share/… link (it can only view stats)

github.howTo1: The repo must be public and belong to the GitHub account you signed in with (or an org where your membership is public).
github.howTo2: We ask for no permissions — we only read the repo's public data.
github.needGithub: Sign in with GitHub first so we can confirm the repo is yours.
